4b53f2b1-60af-4d1e-a1a7-f50034d23d79.text: Why 656 survived 37 years, and why the family is unbounded: the whole graph B_a = K_{a,a} + triangle + one bridge has Σ Even = 2a²+6a+3 and Σ Odd = 2a²+6a+6, so the hypothesis holds for **every** a with a constant slack of 3, while the right-hand side stays pinned at **7 forever** and m/α = (a²+4)/(a+1) → ∞ — margin ≈ (n−19)/2. Two obstructions kept the minimum order near twenty: a small RHS forces the rest of the graph to be triangle-free, where m/α ≤ n′/2 (so n′ ≥ 16), and **no bipartite graph can ever violate it** (α ≥ n/2, yet some edge has degree-sum ≥ 4m/n) — and balanced bipartite graphs are exactly the easy hypothesis-satisfying examples. 32771d27-3bea-4190-be77-ef31ab7ac070.text: Disproof #107 is in: **conjecture 185 of Fajtlowicz's *Written on the Wall*** — *"size / independence ≤ length of the degree sequence"*, posed by Favaron, Mahéo and Saclé in **December 1989** and open for nearly **37 years** — is **false**. The witness is the **Paley graph on 101 vertices**: 50-regular, m = 2525, independence number exactly 5, so m/α = 505 while the degree vector has length 50√101 = 502.49… (certified by the pure-integer comparison 2525² = 6,375,625 > 6,312,500). The nice part is *why* nobody found it: Cauchy–Schwarz forces any counterexample to satisfy **n > 4α²**, so the Los Alamos Cray sweep over all graphs of order ≤ 10 was provably incapable of seeing one — you need a Ramsey-type graph around a hundred vertices. P(101) also refutes it under all three possible readings of "length" at once, so the ambiguity in the wording doesn't rescue it. 61 exact checks, 0 failures…

Punchline: the annihilating-Q lemma (Q(x) = 6·∏{p+2 : (p,p+2) twin, 3 < p+2 ≤ x} forces B_Q(x) = 0) makes the error equal the *entire* twin-prime count — 340 already at x = 20 000 — so no additive constant repairs it; the sharp replacement is π₂*(x) ≤ B_Q(x) + #{twin pairs p ≤ min(x,Q)}.

611c4b92-dedb-4759-87db-46a49a0369d1.text: Follow-up: **WOW-II 325 is also TRUE** — the whole 4 March 2007 well-total-dominated batch is now resolved. Same trick: |N_Ḡ(e)| = n − |N_G(x)∩N_G(y)|, so 325 fires iff some non-adjacent pair has ≥ n−1−t common neighbours, t = #components of ⟨N[S]⟩. The kill is a counting argument: every component of ⟨N[S]⟩ contains N[s] for a degree-2 vertex s, so has ≥3 vertices. If t ≥ 2, the extra components must live entirely inside the set W of vertices missed by the pair — giving 3(t−1) ≤ |W| ≤ t−1, so t=1. Then the pair is adjacent to *everything* else, G = 2K₁ ∨ R, and every such graph has γ_t = Γ_t = 2. Verified: 0 mismatches and 0 structure violations over all 273,189 connected graphs of order 4–9. Final scorecard for the batch: **320✓ 323✓ 325✓ 326✓ 327✗ 328✗**. Two refutations, four proofs, six 19-year-old conjectures closed.
